**What I did:**
- Confirmed [database/mwu_rpee.sqlite](database/mwu_rpee.sqlite) was missing the table
- Ran the existing migration script [scripts/migrate_team_members.php](scripts/migrate_team_members.php), which created it

**Verified:**
- Table now exists with columns `id, application_id, user_id, role, status, invited_at, responded_at`
- Ran the exact query pattern from [ApplicationController.php:256](app/Controllers/ApplicationController.php#L256) (`SELECT tm.*, u.full_name FROM application_team_members tm JOIN users u ... WHERE tm.application_id = ?`) against application id 1 — it executes cleanly and returns an empty result set (no team members assigned yet, which is expected)

The `application_view&id=1` page should load without the exception now.

One thing to be aware of: [database/sqlite_schema.sql](database/sqlite_schema.sql) does **not** include this table, so if you ever rebuild the database from the schema files, you'll need to run `php scripts/migrate_team_members.php` again afterward. Let me know if you'd like me to add the table definition to the base schema so fresh installs get it automatically.

# Feature Implementation Prompt: My Evaluations for Researcher and College Research Coordinator

## 1. Project Context

I am developing the Research Management System (REEP) for a university. The system is built using **PHP, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript only**.

Implement a complete **My Evaluations** feature in the sidebars of these two dashboards:

1. Researcher Dashboard
2. College Research Coordinator Dashboard

The purpose is to allow authorized users to view research proposals assigned to them for evaluation, review the full proposal, submit their evaluation, and provide comments and constructive feedback.

**Important:** Do not create a separate CMS or introduce another technology stack. Integrate the feature into the existing REEP application, database, authentication, authorization, and dashboard layouts.

## 2. Sidebar Integration

Add a sidebar navigation item named **My Evaluations** to both dashboards.

- Researcher Dashboard → My Evaluations
- College Research Coordinator Dashboard → My Evaluations

Use the existing sidebar design, icons, colors, spacing, responsive behavior, and active-navigation styles.

The navigation item must open the existing route:

`/REEP/public/index.php?action=my_evaluations`

Reuse this route and extend its role-based behavior rather than creating duplicate pages or separate evaluation systems.

The System Administrator must not receive this sidebar item or access the My Evaluations page as an evaluator.

## 3. Role-Based Evaluation Workflow

### A. Researcher Dashboard

A researcher may be assigned to evaluate another researcher's proposal at the college or university level.

On the My Evaluations page, the researcher must be able to:

- View all research proposals assigned to them for evaluation.
- Identify the evaluation level: College Level or University Level.
- View the proposal title, principal investigator, college, department, submission date, assignment date, and evaluation deadline where available.
- Open and read the complete research proposal.
- Download the submitted proposal PDF or DOC/DOCX file when available.
- Read the evaluation instructions and assessment criteria applicable to the assignment.
- Enter an evaluation, comments, and constructive feedback.
- Save a draft if the workflow supports drafts.
- Submit the completed evaluation.
- View their previously submitted evaluation and submission status.
- See whether the evaluation is pending, draft, submitted, returned for revision, or overdue, as applicable to the existing workflow.

A researcher must never see proposals assigned exclusively to another evaluator.

### B. College Research Coordinator Dashboard

The College Research Coordinator must have the same My Evaluations page functionality for research proposals assigned to them.

The coordinator must be able to:

- View proposals personally assigned to them for evaluation.
- Identify the college-level evaluation stage.
- Open and read the full proposal and download its attached document.
- Review the applicable evaluation criteria and instructions.
- Record their assessment, comments, and detailed feedback.
- Save a draft when supported.
- Submit the evaluation.
- View their own previously submitted evaluations and their statuses.

**Important distinction:** The coordinator's My Evaluations page is for evaluating proposals personally assigned to the coordinator. It is not the same as the separate workflow for assigning proposals to college evaluators.

Keep the existing proposal assignment functionality separate and intact.

## 4. My Evaluations Page UI

Create a professional, responsive page that follows the existing REEP dashboard design.

At the top, display a page title and a brief description explaining that users can review and evaluate assigned research proposals.

Include summary cards where supported by real database data:

- Total Assigned
- Pending Evaluation
- Submitted Evaluations
- Overdue Evaluations

Provide search, filtering, and sorting capabilities.

Suggested filters:

- Evaluation level
- Evaluation status
- College
- Department
- Assignment date
- Deadline

Display assigned proposals in a clean table or responsive cards with the following fields:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Proposal Title | Title of the assigned research proposal |
| Principal Investigator | Name of the researcher who submitted it |
| College / Department | Proposal owner's academic unit |
| Evaluation Level | College or University |
| Assigned Date | Date assigned to the evaluator |
| Deadline | Evaluation due date, if configured |
| Status | Current evaluation status |
| Action | Open Evaluation / Continue Evaluation / View Evaluation |

Use meaningful empty states when the evaluator has no assignments. Do not display fabricated proposals, statistics, or evaluation records.

## 5. Proposal Review and Evaluation Form

When the user selects a proposal, open a dedicated detail page, modal, or existing application-style review screen.

### Proposal information

Display:

- Proposal title and abstract.
- Principal investigator and co-investigators, where available.
- College and department.
- Research theme or call for proposals, where applicable.
- Uploaded proposal document and download option.
- Submission date.
- Evaluation level.
- Assignment instructions and deadline.
- Relevant supporting documents, if available.

Provide a secure way to open or download the proposal document.

### Evaluation form

The form must support the existing REEP evaluation criteria and workflow.

Include the following where appropriate:

1. **Evaluation criteria:** Display the actual criteria configured for the relevant evaluation stage.
2. **Criterion assessment:** Allow the evaluator to assess each criterion using the existing rating scale, score range, or assessment options.
3. **Criterion comments:** Allow written comments for individual criteria where required.
4. **Overall evaluation:** Record the overall assessment using the valid options defined by the existing workflow.
5. **Strengths:** Identify the proposal's strengths.
6. **Weaknesses and concerns:** Identify weaknesses, gaps, or methodological concerns.
7. **Recommendations:** Provide practical recommendations for improvement.
8. **Overall comments:** Provide a detailed evaluation of the proposal.
9. **Feedback to researcher:** Provide clear, constructive feedback explaining what the researcher should improve.
10. **Final recommendation:** Use only the existing permitted recommendations, such as Pass, Fail, or Revision Required, according to the relevant evaluation stage.

Do not invent a new scoring scale or introduce decision options that conflict with the existing REEP evaluation rules.

If the system already has an evaluation form or criteria configuration, reuse it.

## 6. Saving and Submitting Evaluations

Implement the complete backend and frontend workflow.

- Validate required fields on both the client and server.
- Allow saving drafts if drafts are supported by the current workflow.
- Allow submission only when all required evaluation fields are complete.
- Save evaluation scores, criterion-level comments, overall comments, feedback, recommendation, evaluator ID, proposal ID, evaluation stage, and timestamps as applicable.
- Show clear success or error messages.
- Preserve submitted evaluation data when the page is refreshed.
- Prevent accidental duplicate submissions.
- Provide confirmation before final submission.
- Make submitted evaluations read-only unless the existing workflow explicitly permits editing or reopening.
- Record status transitions and audit information where the application supports them.

Use database transactions where necessary to prevent partially saved evaluations.

## 7. Authorization and Data Security

Implement server-side authorization for every relevant action.

- Only authenticated users with an authorized evaluator role can access My Evaluations.
- The evaluator must have an actual assignment to the requested proposal and evaluation stage.
- A user must not access another evaluator's assignments by changing a URL, proposal ID, or request parameter.
- Only authorized evaluators can create or update their own evaluation records.
- Validate that a submitted evaluation belongs to the correct proposal and evaluation stage.
- Prevent duplicate evaluations for the same assignment unless the existing workflow explicitly allows multiple submissions or revisions.
- Protect state-changing requests using the application's existing CSRF protection.
- Validate uploaded-file access and prevent unauthorized disclosure of research documents.
- Do not expose private evaluator comments or internal committee deliberations to researchers unless the workflow explicitly permits sharing them.

The System Administrator must not be treated as an evaluator merely because they have administrative access.

## 8. Evaluation Workflow Integration

Integrate with the existing REEP research lifecycle.

### College-level evaluation

1. The College Research Coordinator receives or manages proposal assignments according to the existing workflow.
2. Authorized college evaluators review their assigned proposals.
3. Each evaluator submits an assessment and feedback.
4. The coordinator can use the existing college-level decision and approval workflow.
5. Proposals that pass the college evaluation proceed to the next authorized stage.

### University-level evaluation

1. The university evaluation committee is created according to the existing workflow.
2. Authorized committee members review their assigned proposals.
3. Each assigned evaluator submits an assessment and feedback.
4. The authorized committee or decision-maker follows the existing university-level decision process.
5. Failed proposals and appeals continue through the existing appeal workflow.

**Do not allow an individual evaluator's submission to automatically approve or reject a proposal unless the existing workflow explicitly defines that behavior.** Keep individual evaluation, committee decisions, coordinator approval, and director approval separate.

## 9. Researcher Feedback Visibility

After an evaluation is submitted, make feedback visible to the proposal's researcher only when the existing workflow permits feedback disclosure.

Clearly distinguish:

- Feedback intended for the researcher.
- Internal comments intended only for authorized coordinators or committee members.
- Final evaluation decisions.

Do not expose confidential committee discussions or private evaluator notes to the researcher.

If revisions are requested, show the researcher the permitted feedback and the next action they are expected to take.

## 10. Database and Backend Requirements

Before changing the database, inspect the existing schema and identify the tables and relationships for:

- Users and roles.
- Research proposals.
- Evaluation assignments.
- Evaluation criteria.
- Individual evaluations.
- Criterion-level scores and comments.
- Feedback and recommendations.
- Evaluation stages and statuses.
- Audit logs, if available.

Reuse existing tables and relationships wherever possible.

If a required field or relationship is missing, create the smallest compatible migration or schema change. Do not create duplicate evaluation tables or parallel assignment workflows.

Ensure that assignment records distinguish the assigned evaluator, proposal, evaluation stage, and status as required by the existing schema.

Use prepared statements or the application's existing safe database-access methods.

## 11. Testing Requirements

Test the following scenarios:

1. A researcher sees their assigned college-level evaluations.
2. A researcher sees their assigned university-level evaluations.
3. A college coordinator sees proposals personally assigned to them.
4. An evaluator cannot access another evaluator's assignments.
5. An evaluator can open and download an authorized proposal.
6. An evaluator can save a draft if supported.
7. An evaluator can submit a valid evaluation.
8. Invalid or incomplete submissions are rejected.
9. Duplicate submissions are prevented unless explicitly allowed.
10. Submitted evaluations remain available after refreshing the page.
11. Researchers see only feedback authorized for disclosure.
12. College and university decisions follow their existing approval workflows.
13. The System Administrator does not see My Evaluations and cannot use it to evaluate proposals.
14. The page works on desktop, tablet, and mobile devices.
15. Existing proposal assignment, appeals, and approval functionality continues to work.

## 12. Implementation Instructions

Start by inspecting the current codebase, including:

- Dashboard sidebar components or shared sidebar templates.
- `/REEP/public/index.php` routing and the `my_evaluations` action.
- Authentication and role checks.
- Research proposal and assignment tables.
- Existing evaluation forms and feedback pages.
- College and university approval workflows.
- CSS and JavaScript conventions.

Then implement the feature across the necessary frontend, PHP backend, and database components.

Do not replace working features unnecessarily. Do not hardcode sample data, fabricate evaluation records, or introduce a new framework.

### Required deliverables

1. My Evaluations sidebar item for both dashboards.
2. Role-aware My Evaluations page using the existing route.
3. Assigned proposal listing, search, and filtering.
4. Secure proposal detail and document access.
5. Complete evaluation form with comments and feedback.
6. Draft and submission handling where supported.
7. Database changes only where necessary.
8. Correct integration with college and university evaluation workflows.
9. Server-side authorization and validation.
10. A test report identifying files changed, database changes, tests performed, and any remaining issues.

### Stop conditions

Do not claim the feature is complete if the page is only a static UI, the evaluation is not persisted, assignments are not checked server-side, or the feedback does not integrate with the existing workflow.

If the current schema or business rules are unclear, inspect the relevant implementation first and report the exact uncertainty before making incompatible assumptions.

**Final objective:** Both researchers and college research coordinators must have a secure, functional My Evaluations page where they can see the research proposals assigned to them, review the full proposals, evaluate them using the correct criteria, and submit meaningful comments and feedback while preserving REEP's existing approval and authorization rules.

#!/bin/bash
# MWU RPEE — END-TO-END ACCEPTANCE TEST (spec §35 — all 44 steps)
#
# Admin creates org + accounts → researcher profile → proposal → coordinator
# screens → two evaluators created + assigned → evaluations → revision →
# re-evaluation → college approval → directorate → university committee →
# funding recommendation → directorate budget approval → agreement issued →
# researcher signs → research ACTIVE → progress → final report → completion →
# archive → audit history.
#
# Run from the project root with the dev server on 127.0.0.1:8099:
#   php -S 127.0.0.1:8099 -t public
#   bash scripts/e2e_acceptance.sh
set -u
[ -f app/bootstrap.php ] || { echo "Run from the project root"; exit 2; }

B=http://127.0.0.1:8099
P='Password123!'
PASS=0; FAIL=0

say()  { printf '%s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { PASS=$((PASS+1)); say "  PASS: $*"; }
bad()  { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); say "  FAIL: $*"; }
chk()  { if [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then ok "$1 ($2)"; else bad "$1 — expected $3 got $2"; fi; }

login() { # email jar -> login http code
  local jar=$2 tok
  rm -f "$jar"
  tok=$(curl -s -m 15 -c "$jar" "$B/login.php" | grep -o 'name="_csrf" value="[^"]*"' | head -1 | sed 's/.*value="//;s/"//')
  curl -s -m 20 -b "$jar" -c "$jar" -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -d "identifier=$1&password=$P&_csrf=$tok" "$B/login.php?action=do_login"
}
tok() { curl -s -m 15 -b "$1" -c "$1" "$B/index.php" | grep -o 'name="csrf-token" content="[^"]*"\|name="_csrf" value="[^"]*"' | head -1 | sed 's/.*content="//;s/.*value="//;s/"//'; }
post() { # jar action data... -> http code
  local jar=$1 action=$2; shift 2
  curl -s -m 20 -b "$jar" -c "$jar" -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$B/index.php?action=$action" "$@"
}
up() { # jar action file extra... -> http code (multipart)
  local jar=$1 action=$2 f=$3; shift 3
  local wf; wf=$(cygpath -m "$f" 2>/dev/null || echo "$f")
  curl -s -m 20 -b "$jar" -c "$jar" -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -F "document=@$wf;type=application/pdf" "$B/index.php?action=$action" "$@"

           )",
        [$roleName]
    );
    echo '  + research.evaluate for ' . $roleName . ($done ? " granted\n" : " already granted\n");
}

echo "Migration completed.\n";
